public_rationale: Learned imitation is a documented feature of GPT training, and TruthfulQA provides evidence that it can produce false answers. That supports Marcus's proposed mechanism. It does not establish that stylistic imitation explains the novel, inappropriate combination in this example. The available research itself distinguishes imitation-driven errors from other failures, so the stronger causal attribution remains unsettled.
limitations: A narrower statement that GPT learns to imitate human text would be supported.
The metaphor does not specify a precise causal mechanism.
Failure to trace this example is not evidence that imitation played no role.

our_interpretation: King of pastiche is an explanatory metaphor, not a measurable ranking against other systems.
The testable reading is that learned imitation of human text explains fluent but inappropriate combinations like the illustrated churro-surgery response.
This does not require literal copying of a training passage, nor does it automatically imply that GPT-3 has no reasoning abilities.
Evidence that the model was trained on human text supports the proposed mechanism but does not by itself identify the cause of the illustrated kind of error.
